headline: Coordinating Fjord and Mountain Peak Access
reservation: While the highway is a public route, specific stops like the Sea to Sky Gondola or provincial parks such as Garibaldi require separate day-use passes or tickets during peak periods. Access systems for popular hiking trails often change seasonally; verify current requirements with BC Parks before arrival. Parking at major viewpoints is not guaranteed and requires early arrival during summer months.

days.title: Fjords and Waterfalls

stops.name: Shannon Falls Provincial Park
stops.detail: Observe the third-highest waterfall in British Columbia via a short forest walk from the highway.

stops.name: Sea to Sky Gondola
stops.detail: Ascend to the summit for views of Howe Sound and the surrounding Coast Mountains from the Sky Pilot Suspension Bridge.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours from Vancouver to Squamish; conditions vary with traffic.
days.note: Expect heavy traffic exiting Vancouver during morning rush hours and weekends.

days.title: Granite Peaks and Alpine Valleys

stops.name: Stawamus Chief Provincial Park
stops.detail: View the massive granite monolith popular with climbers or hike the trails for elevated vistas of the Squamish valley.

stops.name: Brandywine Falls Provincial Park
stops.detail: Stop for a short walk to see the spectacular 70-meter waterfall and the basalt columns of the Cheakamus River.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the stretch between Squamish and Whistler; conditions vary.
days.note: Parking at Stawamus Chief is limited; have a secondary plan if the lot is full.

days.title: Glacial Vistas and Olympic Legacy

stops.name: Whistler Village
stops.detail: Explore the pedestrian-only base of Whistler Blackcomb, featuring local art, dining, and the Olympic Plaza.

stops.name: Nairn Falls Provincial Park
stops.detail: Travel just north of Whistler to witness the Green River carving through a narrow rock canyon.

days.driving: Allow 30-45 minutes for local exploration; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: Mountain weather can change rapidly; check the local forecast before heading north of Whistler.

intel.title: Trailhead Limitations
intel.text: Popular spots like Shannon Falls and the Stawamus Chief lots often reach capacity by mid-morning on weekends. Use overflow lots in Squamish if available.

intel.title: Mountain Terrain Obstructions
intel.text: Cellular signal is generally strong along the highway but can drop significantly in deep valleys or on higher elevation hiking trails.

intel.title: Major Hub Services
intel.text: Fuel and electric charging stations are located in Vancouver, Squamish, and Whistler. There are long stretches between these hubs without service stations.

intel.title: Rush Hour Congestion
intel.text: Friday afternoons and Sunday evenings see significant delays for travelers returning to Vancouver. Adjust travel times to avoid peak commuter periods.

intel.title: Winter Tire Regulations
intel.text: From October 1 to March 31, winter tires or chains are legally required for travel north of Horseshoe Bay. Check current BC Ministry of Transportation mandates.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental vehicle at Vancouver International Airport (YVR) and secure outdoor supplies in North Vancouver before joining Highway 99 North.
plan.vehicle: Reliable brakes and engines are necessary for steep grades; check rental policies regarding winter tire compliance for the route.
plan.goldenHour: Tantalus Lookout for sunset views of the ice-capped Tantalus Range across the valley, noting seasonal sun position changes.
